label: Abdication
summary: A saved-scope name (abdication) that the base game's script never uses.
details: The game documents nothing about it, so what it holds is not known from the available information.

label: Accolade
summary: The accolade (an honor held by a knight) that the script is working with.
details: For accolade icons the game itself gives the accolade the icon is for under this name, while the root there is the accolade's type. Vanilla also reads it often (309 times) in the accolade script values and accolade effects, where it holds the accolade being handled.

label: Accolade type
summary: The primary attribute (kind) of the accolade being handled.
details: Vanilla uses it only in the accolade name files, in the conditions that pick a name; the game's own notes there say it is meant for option triggers, not for text.

label: Active obligation
summary: A saved-scope name (active obligation) that the base game's script never uses.
details: The game documents nothing about it, so what it holds is not known from the available information.

label: Activity
summary: The activity (a feast, a hunt, a pilgrimage and so on) that the script is running for.
details: The game itself gives it in the activity files: in activity locales and in an activity type's checks, such as whether the activity may go on, where the root is often the activity too. Next to it the game gives `scope:host`, the character hosting the activity. Vanilla reads it very often (11,214 times).

label: Activity intent
summary: A saved scope used in one Royal Court wedding event, where a comment says the event gains opinion with it.
details: Vanilla uses it once, in a wedding event of the Royal Court expansion. The game's own comment there speaks of gaining opinion with it, which suggests a character; the game documents nothing more.

label: Actor
summary: The character who starts a character interaction.
details: The game itself gives it in every part of a character interaction: its background, whether it is available or valid, and its redirect effect, which may swap the actor for another character. In decisions the game gives the current actor under this name too, when it fills the list of choices in the player's window. Vanilla reads it about 12,700 times, mostly in interaction files.

label: Added doctrines
summary: The doctrines that a rite change added.
details: Used in the code on_action that fires when a rite is changed; the game's comment calls it a list of the doctrines the change added to the rite. A matching list holds the removed ones.

label: Added tenets
summary: The tenets that a rite change added.
details: Used in the code on_action that fires when a rite is changed; the game's comment calls it a list of the tenets the change added to the rite. A matching list holds the removed ones.

label: Age
summary: A number compared with ages such as 16 when the game decides on clothing.
details: Vanilla reads it 8 times, all in the clothing triggers, for example to keep children under 16 without headgear. Whose age it holds is not shown.

label: Agent
summary: A character acting as an agent; in schemes, the agent that was just discovered.
details: The game itself sets it in the `on_scheme_agent_discovered` on_action (with the scheme as root), so script can tell which agent was found out. Vanilla also saves characters under this name in other places, such as feast events and councillor spouse intrigue events (101 uses in all), and there who it is depends on the event.

label: Agent slot
summary: The scheme agent slot being handled.
details: Vanilla reads it 15 times, in the invite-agent-to-scheme interaction and a Roads to Power story cycle event, where it is passed to the add-to-agent-slot effect and to a check of whether someone is valid as an agent in that slot.

label: AI boldness
summary: A saved-scope name (ai boldness) that the base game's script never uses.
details: The game documents nothing about it, so what it holds is not known from the available information.

label: AI vengefulness
summary: A saved-scope name (ai vengefulness) that the base game's script never uses.
details: The game documents nothing about it, so what it holds is not known from the available information.

label: AI zeal
summary: A saved-scope name (ai zeal) that the base game's script never uses.
details: The game documents nothing about it, so what it holds is not known from the available information.

label: Ally
summary: A character who is an ally of the one being checked.
details: Vanilla reads it 10 times. In the AI's call-an-ally action it is saved temporarily while going through each ally of the character, and the action checks whether that ally can be called into the war.

label: Appointment
summary: The title that was just given by appointment, in an admin event.
details: Vanilla saves it once, in a Roads to Power admin event, on a held title whose history shows an appointment in the last day. The same place saves the succession and conquest versions instead, depending on which happened.

label: Appointment succession
summary: The title whose governor changed by appointment succession in the last day, in an admin event.
details: Vanilla saves it once, in a Roads to Power admin event, on a held title whose history shows an appointment succession in the last day. The event checks that it exists.

label: Appointment trait override
summary: A saved-scope name (appointment trait override) that the base game's script never uses.
details: The game documents nothing about it, so what it holds is not known from the available information.

label: Army
summary: The army that an on_action or event is about.
details: Vanilla reads it 62 times, in the army and combat on_actions. Which army it is depends on what the game was doing when it saved it.

label: Army owner
summary: The character who owns the army that someone is to command.
details: Vanilla reads it 21 times, in the scripted rules and war and peace triggers. The game's comment in the scripted rules calls it who owns the army to command.

label: Artifact
summary: The artifact (a collectible item such as a weapon or a book) that the script is working with.
details: The game itself gives it in the artifact templates (whether a character can equip, fully benefit from, reforge or repair this artifact, with the character as root), when a relic is enshrined at a holy site (the faith is root), and in artifact visuals (the owner is root, this is the artifact being made). Schemes get it too. Vanilla also saves artifacts under this name in its own script, such as feast pulse actions (269 uses in all).

label: Artifacts
summary: The artifacts being enshrined when a holy site is created.
details: The game's comment on the holy site created on_action and on the scripted costs calls it a list of the artifacts being enshrined.

label: Attacker
summary: The character who attacks in a casus belli (a justification for war).
details: Vanilla reads it 3,913 times, mostly in casus belli type files, where the game's notes call it the primary attacker.

label: Attackers
summary: A saved-scope name (attackers) that the base game's script never uses.
details: The game documents nothing about it, so what it holds is not known from the available information.

label: Barony
summary: The barony (the smallest kind of title) that the script is working with, such as the one picked in a holy order decision.
details: In decisions that show a barony picker (founding a holy order, revoking a holy order's lease) the game gives the barony the player picked under this name. Vanilla's own script also saves baronies under it elsewhere, for example in a major decision for East Europe (229 uses in all).

label: Barter loot
summary: The loot a bartering army gained.
details: In the barter on_actions it is added as gold to the army's owner when loot is delivered; when the army is defeated it is how much loot they carried.

label: Barterer
summary: The character who owns the bartering army.
details: Vanilla reads it 15 times, in the barter on_actions, where the game's comment calls it the person owning the bartering army.

label: Base character
summary: The character a pool character selector picks or creates a new character for, usually the council owner or the predecessor.
details: The game always sets it in pool character selectors, while root is the pool character being judged. The selector's settings read from it: `pool = faith` searches pool characters of its faith, `court = yes` adds its court's courtiers, `culture = character` uses its culture, and the clergy gender follows its rite. When the game makes a holder for a granted title, it is the new liege.

label: Base value
summary: A number that gets added to the AI's score for a candidate for a court position.
details: Vanilla reads it 56 times, in the court position type files, for example adding it to a candidate score that starts at 100. Where the number comes from is not shown.

label: Blackmailer
summary: The character who is blackmailing someone.
details: Vanilla reads it 3 times, in the scripted rules and the blackmail events. Meaning inferred from the name and those files.

label: Bloc
summary: A bloc that members are added to.
details: Vanilla reads it 58 times, in the title on_actions and the house bloc scripted effects, for example adding a member to it with the add-confederation-member effect. Which bloc it is depends on the script that saved it.

label: Can afford current level
summary: Whether the character can still afford a legend's current level.
details: Vanilla uses it once, in the legends values: when it is no, the AI's score for completing the legend rises by 100.

label: Can afford personal MaA
summary: Whether the ruler can afford the initial buy cost of any personal men-at-arms unit.
details: Vanilla reads it 3 times, in the scripted rule about the ruler considering hiring men-at-arms (a ruler's soldiers); the rule's comment describes it this way.

label: Candidate
summary: A character being considered for something; in elections, the candidate an elector is weighing.
details: In elective succession the game gives the candidate being considered under this name, with the elector as root and `scope:title` as the title being elected. Vanilla also saves candidates under it elsewhere, such as important actions and the Mongol invasion effects (704 uses in all), and what they are a candidate for depends on the script that saved it.

label: Casus belli type
summary: The type of casus belli (justification for war) being looked at.
details: Vanilla reads it twice, in the AI conqueror effects. Meaning inferred from the name and that file.

label: CB prestige factor
summary: A number the casus belli uses as the base of the prestige (fame) it gives.
details: Vanilla reads it 54 times, in casus belli type files such as claim and de jure war. In the claim file it feeds the fame base, and a comment says it is set by the claim casus belli setup.

label: Changed obligations
summary: A list the game gives while a subject contract is being changed: every contract obligation changed in the window.
details: Available when modifying a subject contract, together with `scope:new_value`. Vanilla's own script does not read it.

label: Changed tenet status
summary: The tenets whose status changed when a rite was updated.
details: Set by the game in the rite updated on_action. The game's comment calls it a list of tenets that had their status changed without being made core or removed from core.

label: Changed tenets or doctrines
summary: Set when a rite update changed tenets or doctrines.
details: Set by the game in the rite updated on_action. It is not set when only looks changed. Vanilla checks that it exists.

label: Changed top liege
summary: A saved-scope name (changed top liege) that the base game's script never uses.
details: The game documents nothing about it, so what it holds is not known from the available information.

label: Character
summary: A character that the script is working with; who it is changes with the place.
details: The game gives a character under this name in many places, each with its own meaning: the character who gets a triggered animation in an activity window, the character who paid for a building's construction (if known), the character diverging a culture's look, and a culture's head when innovations are weighed. Vanilla's own script saves still others under it (787 uses), so check where it is set.

label: Character converted
summary: A saved-scope name (character converted) that the base game's script never uses.
details: The game documents nothing about it, so what it holds is not known from the available information.

label: Characters
summary: A saved-scope name (characters) that the base game's script never uses.
details: The game documents nothing about it, so what it holds is not known from the available information.

label: Checking native language
summary: Whether the AI is scoring its own language.
details: Vanilla reads it 5 times, in the culture script values and the scripted rules, where a comment describes it this way. It is compared with yes and no.

label: Child
summary: A child that the script is working with.
details: Vanilla reads it 2,144 times. In the child birth on_actions the game's comment calls it the newborn character; in other places, such as the education important actions, which child it is depends on the script that saved it.

label: Claimant
summary: The character who holds the claim in a claim-based casus belli.
details: Vanilla reads it 263 times, in casus belli types such as claim and event war. The game's notes say it may be unset.

label: Combat
summary: The combat itself.
details: Vanilla reads it 7 times, in the dynamic script values, where the comment calls it the combat itself (for example for the gold the winning side gains).

label: Combat enemy side
summary: A saved-scope name (combat enemy side) that the base game's script never uses.
details: The game documents nothing about it, so what it holds is not known from the available information.

label: Combat side
summary: The side of a combat that the character or commander is on.
details: Vanilla reads it 105 times, in the combat phase events for commanders and knights; the game's comments call it the side of combat the character is on. Vanilla reaches the other side from it with enemy_side.

label: Commanders
summary: A saved-scope name (commanders) that the base game's script never uses.
details: The game documents nothing about it, so what it holds is not known from the available information.

label: Concubine
summary: The character who is a concubine in the situation the script handles.
details: Vanilla reads it 14 times, in the tributary interactions and the marriage important actions. Meaning inferred from the name and those files.

label: Confederation
summary: The confederation that is being joined.
details: Vanilla reads it 20 times, in the confederation types and on_actions; a comment there calls it the confederation that is being joined.

label: Conquest
summary: The title that was just taken by conquest, in an admin event.
details: Vanilla saves it in a Roads to Power admin event on a held title whose history shows a conquest in the last day, and reads it in a debug interaction too.
